"The.. what?" She takes the copy and starts reading it. "What exactly is all of this for?"
"A new system of government. When we win the war, we don't want someone else to come in and act as King."

Ferrah smiles, and her pale blue complexion fades to a more pleasant light brown. "Thank you, Finn Midask. I appreciate the honesty." She pauses for a moment. "You're really in this now. Are you committed to fight for your beliefs and those of these people for as long as you are able? Putting your name on it's a big responsibility."
"So, you want someone to rule... but not be a king..." She speaks a little slow as if she's still to wrap her head around the concept.
"Not a single person, a council of sorts. A truly representative government, something we never got from King George."
"The goal is to keep power in check, give a voice to the people, all people, through elections and voting."

"Fighting red coats has always been natural. I like many others, never got a choice. This is something I believe in wholeheartedly. 

I don't hold faith in any religious beings, but I do hold my faith in people. People want the best for themselves *and* each other. I believe that it's the people that will see through this government that I will never get to see truly grow. I fight passionately for this because I want those after me to have their best chance at leading successful and happy lives. "
"So... it's a system that allows everyone to have a voice?" She tilts her head a little.
She smiles and nods

***A QUICK GUIDE TO RESTORATIVE JUSTICE:***
```
Definition: a system of criminal justice which focuses on the rehabilitation of offenders through reconciliation with victims and the community at large. 

• Seeks to repair the harm done
• Emphasizes accountability, making amends, and if agreed upon, facilitated meeting between offenders and victims.
• Seeks to empower victims and meet their needs
• The goal is to heal, and prevent repeat offenders from being cycled through the system
• Often applies indigenous practices of council and justice when dealing out consequences
• If needed, a prison would be used for reintegration into society by giving them tools to succeed
• Community restoration and involvement is key to success 

Examples:
• Community service 
• Restitution 
• Victim-offender reconciliation```
